note: mapping_basis=data_labels, no inference in the code->text tie: data/goldberg_2018_escs.py melts PRS.tab with var_name="item" and renames nothing (BLOCK_NAMES maps prefix ("prs","music") only to the table suffix music_preferences), so the live codes music1..music22 ARE the .tab column names (core model s3 pattern 1). The DDI <labl level="variable"> of each music column names the genre; DDI labels = PRS_items.txt MUSIC list = PRS.pdf p.8 MUSIC grid read column-wise (Alternative..Funk = music1..8, Gospel..Opera = music9..15, Pop..Soundtracks/theme songs = music16..22), 22/22 in order. Deviations, all disclosed: (1) item_text equals the printed form and the DDI label 22/22; DDI labels carry trailing spaces ("Country    ", "Funk ", "Oldies   "), stripped; the form line-wraps "International/ foreign" and "Soundtracks/ theme songs", joined without a space as in the DDI label and PRS_items.txt. (2) option_text follows the printed scale box (Dislike Strongly / Dislike Moderately / Dislike a Little / Neither like nor dislike / Like a Little / Like Moderately / Like Strongly = 1..7 over the numbered bubbles) rather than the DDI value labels, which are lowercase, abbreviate 4 as "neither" and misspell "dislike moderatly"; the processing script stores the .tab integers unchanged and the DDI value labels tie the same 1..7 direction, so resp equals the bubble number. Every item uses all 7 levels in the live data. (3) instructions is the page's intro paragraph, which covers all four leisure blocks (music, books/magazines, movies, television) on the form; the block heading "MUSIC" is carried in instrument. Missing responses are meaningful per the instructions ("If you haven't heard of one, leave it blank").
